# shop configuration

Generated by docuconf from the configuration contract of `shop`, written by hand (`hand-written` `1.0.0`) for an image no docuconf SDK built. Do not edit this file: change the contract, then run `docuconf docs`.

`shop` reads 20 environment variables and 1 file. 4 are required, 2 only under a condition, and 3 are secret.

The image runs as roles `web` or `worker`, one per workload: the platform sets `DOCUCONF_ROLE` to the workload's role, and an input marked with roles is used only in those.

It includes the well-known fragment `otel@1`: variables a runtime or library reads rather than the app's own code, which the platform may set.

## Contents

**[Environment variables](#environment-variables)**

- [`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](#allowed_origins): Origins the web server accepts browser requests from (required, `web` only)
- [`DATABASE_URL`](#database_url): Postgres connection string (required, secret)
- [`DOCUCONF_ROLE`](#docuconf_role): The role this workload runs: web or worker (required)
- [`LOG_FORMAT`](#log_format): Log output format
- [`LOG_SCHEMA_URL`](#log_schema_url): JSON schema the structured logs follow (required when `LOG_FORMAT` is `json`)
- [`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`](#otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint): Base URL of the OTLP collector
- [`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`](#otel_exporter_otlp_headers): Headers sent with every OTLP export, comma-separated key=value pairs (secret)
- [`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`](#otel_exporter_otlp_protocol): Transport protocol for OTLP export
- [`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`](#otel_logs_exporter): Log exporters, comma-separated, such as otlp or none
- [`OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`](#otel_metrics_exporter): Metric exporters, comma-separated, such as otlp or none
- [`OTEL_PROPAGATORS`](#otel_propagators): Context propagators, comma-separated, such as tracecontext,baggage
- [`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`](#otel_resource_attributes): Resource attributes, comma-separated key=value pairs
- [`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`](#otel_sdk_disabled): Disable the OpenTelemetry SDK entirely
- [`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`](#otel_service_name): Service name reported in telemetry
- [`OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`](#otel_traces_exporter): Trace exporters, comma-separated, such as otlp or none
- [`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`](#otel_traces_sampler): Sampler for traces
- [`OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`](#otel_traces_sampler_arg): Argument for the sampler, such as the ratio for traceidratio
- [`PORT`](#port): Port the web server listens on (`web` only)
- [`QUEUES`](#queues): Queues the worker takes jobs from, in priority order (required, `worker` only)
- [`WEBHOOKS_ENABLED`](#webhooks_enabled): Send order webhooks to partners (`worker` only)

**[Files](#files)**

- [`webhook-signing-key`](#webhook-signing-key): Key that signs outgoing order webhooks (required when `WEBHOOKS_ENABLED` is `true`, `worker` only, secret)

## Files

The platform mounts each file at its path; the app reads it there. With `DOCUCONF_FILE_ROOT=./dev`, the SDK reads every path under `./dev` instead, for local runs.

### `webhook-signing-key`

Key that signs outgoing order webhooks

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `text` (text file) |
| Required | only when [`WEBHOOKS_ENABLED`](#webhooks_enabled) is `true` |
| Roles | only `worker`: other workloads do not set it |
| Secret | yes: never write its value in code, docs or a values file |
| Path | `/etc/shop/webhooks/signing.key` |
| Contents | a UTF-8 text file |
| Reload | `restart`: the app reads the file at startup; a changed source needs a rollout |
| Constraints | at least 32 characters (Unicode code points) |
| Sources | `secret`, `csi`, `injected` (the injector writes the file at the path) |
| Boot errors | `out_of_range`, `file_missing`, `file_unreadable`, `file_malformed` |

## Sources

Where the platform may get each input from, as named in the tables above. A secret comes only from a secret store or an injector.

- `literal`: a literal value in the platform's values file
- `injected`: supplied when the container starts by an injector (`injected`), such as Bank-Vaults, `op run` or the Vault Agent injector; checked at boot
- `secretKeyRef`: a key of a Kubernetes Secret (`secretKeyRef`)
- `configMapKeyRef`: a key of a ConfigMap (`configMapKeyRef`), checked at boot
- `fieldRef`: a pod field from the Downward API (`fieldRef`), such as `metadata.namespace`
- `resourceFieldRef`: a container resource limit or request (`resourceFieldRef`), such as `limits.memory`
- `secret`: a Kubernetes Secret (`secret`), one key per file
- `csi`: the Secrets Store CSI driver (`csi`)

## Boot errors

At boot the SDK checks every input and reports all problems together, one line each, with one of these codes. Secret values never appear in the messages.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `missing_required` | A required input is not set, and has no default. | Set it through one of its allowed sources. |
| `invalid_type` | The value does not parse as the input's type in its wire format, or a secret still holds an unresolved injector reference (`vault:`, `op://`, `ref+`). | Write the value in the input's wire format. For an injected secret, make sure the injector runs. |
| `out_of_range` | A number, duration, length, list item or key is outside the input's bounds; an empty key always is. | Use a value within the input's constraints. |
| `not_in_enum` | The value is not one of the allowed values. | Use one of the listed values, spelled exactly as listed. |
| `invalid_scheme` | The URL's scheme is not one of the allowed schemes. | Use a URL with an allowed scheme. |
| `file_missing` | The file is not at its path. | Give the input a source, and check that it is mounted at the declared path (or that its path variable points at it). |
| `file_unreadable` | The file exists but cannot be read. | Check the mount, the file mode and the user the app runs as. |
| `file_malformed` | The file does not parse in its format, is a directory, is not UTF-8 text, or holds too few certificates. | Fix the content so it parses in the declared format. |
